notes: The yellow of the St David's cross, as the twin of the red and green default. The red is oklch(0.489 0.198 25.4) and the gold is oklch(0.887 0.18 95.3): almost the same chroma (about 0.18 to 0.20), 70 degrees round the hue wheel, so they sit together as a pair. Every green is unchanged. Where the default uses red, this uses the gold: the top bar and tiles are the gold with the dark green ink on them (the red used near-white text, because red is dark and gold is light). Light accent: the same lightness as the red (0.489), at the most chroma yellow allows there (0.10), so it reads as text with the same contrast the red does. Dark accent: the brightest gold, the counterpart of the default's ring red. The dark neutrals keep the default's lightness and chroma and take the gold's hue (95.3) in place of the red's (17 to 29). Not colour-blind safe: it makes no colour-vision promise. Key-word colours (key-1 to key-3): a blue, an orange or gold and a purple, found by a search for the colourful end of what keeps the level's text contrast on the page and the card and stays at least 0.12 apart, and from the ink, in OKLab as seen with normal, protan, deutan and tritan vision. Revised 2026-10-28 for consistency in OKLCH: every colour is written in OKLCH (the dark background and the dark ink, which were hex, now are oklch(0.187 0.034 175)); the green tint of the neutrals is hue 175 in dark as in light (the dark ones had taken the yellow's hue, 95.3); and the key-word colours keep one hue each in light and dark, a blue (260), a red-orange (25) and a violet (315), with only the lightness changing, so a word keeps its colour when the appearance changes. The old orange key (hue 95) was indistinguishable from the olive-gold accent (OKLab distance 0.011), so the three keys were searched for at least 0.13 from the accent (the Safe scheme's included), from the ink and from each other, with the level's text contrast and under simulated colour blindness.
